summary: Bradshaw Army Airfield is a U.S. military installation situated on the high-elevation slopes of Mauna Kea on Hawaii's Big Island, near the town of Waimea (Kamuela). At roughly 6,190 feet above sea level, it supports training operations for the U.S. Army and serves as a staging point for activities at the nearby Pohakuloa Training Area. The airfield is not open to commercial aviation and is primarily used for military and government purposes.
faqs:
Q: Is Bradshaw Army Airfield open to commercial flights?
A: No, BSF/PHSF is a military airfield and does not offer scheduled commercial passenger service. Travelers should use Kona International Airport (KOA) or Hilo International Airport (ITO) instead.

Q: Why is the airport located at such a high elevation?
A: The airfield sits on the upper slopes of Mauna Kea at about 6,190 feet, which provides cooler temperatures and strategic positioning for military training and operations in central Hawaii.

Q: What facilities are available at Bradshaw Army Airfield?
A: The facility primarily supports military aircraft and personnel. Public amenities such as rental cars, food, and retail are not available, and civilian access is restricted.

Q: Can private pilots land at Bradshaw Army Airfield?
A: Landing at BSF generally requires prior military authorization. Private and general aviation operators should coordinate with the controlling authority well in advance.
transport_tips: Since Bradshaw Army Airfield is not open to civilian travelers, visitors heading to the Waimea area should fly into Kona International Airport (KOA) or Hilo International Airport (ITO) and rent a car for the approximately 45-minute drive. The Saddle Road (Hawaii Route 200) connects Hilo to Waimea and passes near Pohakuloa Training Area. Having a personal vehicle is highly recommended, as public transportation options in this rural part of the Big Island are limited.
